concepts.title: Faxian's Pilgrimage as Vinaya Archaeology
concepts.excerpt: Imagine you're a monk in 5th-century China. Your monastery has the sutras — the doctrinal teaching is fine.

concepts.title: Vinaya Textual Archaeology — Faxian's Mahasanghika Discovery
concepts.excerpt: In 399 CE Faxian leaves Ch'ang-gan with a question: where in the Buddhist world is the written Vinaya still preserved?

concepts.title: Mathura Gupta Polity — Faxian's Snapshot (c. 405 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Faxian crosses the Indus in 404 CE, walks south-east through Mathura, and writes down what he sees on the ground.

concepts.title: Metal-Plate Land Grants as Monastic Economic Foundation
concepts.excerpt: Buddhism had a problem the early Christian church also had and the early Islamic ummah also had: how do you make an institution that survives the death of its founder by more than a generation?

concepts.title: Public Hospital System — Gupta Pataliputra (Faxian's Witness)
concepts.excerpt: You walk into Pataliputra in 405 CE — the old Mauryan capital, "the cities and towns of this country are the greatest of all in the Middle Kingdom" — and you see something you would not see in Constantinople, in Damascus, in Chang'an, or in any other contemporary metropolis.

concepts.title: Faxian's Asokan Inscription Paraphrase
concepts.excerpt: Three le south of Pataliputra in 405 CE, Faxian stands in front of a stone pillar.

concepts.title: Chandala Wood-Block Warning Caste Architecture
concepts.excerpt: You are walking into Mathura in the early 5th century. The streets are quiet.

concepts.title: Monastic Hospitality Protocol — International (Faxian)
concepts.excerpt: You have been walking for fourteen days. The road from Tamalipti to the next monastery is dusty.

concepts.title: Specialized Relic Cults by Monastic Sub-Community
concepts.excerpt: Walk into a typical large Buddhist monastery in 5th-century-CE India and you will not see one shrine to the Buddha and a generic veneration pattern.

concepts.title: Prasenajit's Gosirsha Chandana Buddha Image — The Iconogenesis Legend
concepts.excerpt: Buddha is gone. He has ascended to the Trayastrimsas heaven of the thirty-three gods to preach the Dharma to his mother Maya, who has been reborn there since dying seven days after his birth.

concepts.title: Buddha's Alms-Bowl as Judge of Virtue — Purushapura
concepts.excerpt: You are a king of the Yueh-she — the Indo-Scythian or Tukharian peoples north of the Indus.

concepts.title: Devadatta Sectarians Still Existing — Faxian's Witness
concepts.excerpt: In 405 CE at Sravasti, Faxian writes a single sentence that should be more famous than it is: "There are also companies of the followers of Devadatta still existing.

concepts.title: Second Council at Vaisali — Weapons Laid Down Tope (Faxian's Witness)
concepts.excerpt: Faxian arrives at Vaisali in 405 CE. He has just crossed the Ganges. He is now in the kingdom whose oligarchic Lichchhavi rulers were among the Buddha's earliest political patrons.

concepts.title: Asoka's 84,000 Topes Project — Faxian's Witness
concepts.excerpt: Right after Buddha's cremation, his body-relics were divided into eight portions and distributed among eight kingdoms whose representatives had gathered to make claims.

concepts.title: Faxian's Three Restrained Emotional Moments
concepts.excerpt: You read most of Faxian's Record of Buddhist Kingdoms and you wouldn't know there was a person inside it.

concepts.title: Tao-ching's Frontier-Land Vow — Permanent Migration
concepts.excerpt: Faxian walks from Ch'ang-gan to Pataliputra for a sack of disciplinary books.

concepts.title: Faxian's Typhoon Salvage Priority — Books and Images
concepts.excerpt: The ship is going down. It's been three days since they left Ceylon. The wind has turned against them.

concepts.title: Faxian Witness vs Hearsay Epistemic Discipline
concepts.excerpt: That single sentence is the discipline.

concepts.title: Legge's 1886 Buddhism Population Revisionism
concepts.excerpt: The Introduction to Legge's 1886 translation of Faxian contains a remarkable third section — pages 196-220 of the source — that has nothing to do with Faxian and everything to do with the religious-statistical politics of late-19th-century Anglo-Protestant scholarship.

concepts.title: Legge's Translator Discipline — Inter-Translator Disagreements
concepts.excerpt: Halfway through Faxian's chronicle, at Ch. XXVI line 1216, Faxian records the death of Ananda — Buddha's beloved cousin, the disciple whose memory preserved most of the Sutras.

concepts.title: Ashokan Pillars as Architectural Innovation
concepts.excerpt: Walk up to the surviving Ashokan pillar at Lauriya-Nandangarh in north Bihar.

concepts.title: Library as Immortality Infrastructure (Orlean)
concepts.excerpt: The underlying theme of The Library Book — what Orlean was actually writing about when she was nominally writing about the 1986 fire that burned 400,000 books and damaged 700,000 more in the LA Central Library — is memory and permanence.
